clue.text: Compare this with instability of mood

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching an adjective describing feeling or ambience

indicators.note: instability means being unsettled, so the letters of the two words before it are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to contrast a thing with mood swings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compare this with instability' reads like an instruction to contrast; really the eleven letters of COMPARE THIS are rearranged, and 'with' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative that creates a distinctive feeling or ambience can be described this way, so it relates to mood.

clue.text: Bother setting apart sides in toss? Here's one

indicators.note: setting apart means pushing two things away from each other, so the outer letters are separated by what goes between
the sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to bother someone is to ail or trouble them

explanation.surface: A coin-tosser wonders whether to keep the two faces apart when flipping.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue's own word 'toss': 'Here's one' means here is one side of a toss.
explanation.definitionFit: When a coin is flipped the caller chooses heads or the reverse face, so this is one of the two outcomes.

clue.text: Oil producer checking Utah's weather?

indicators.note: checking here means holding back or restraining, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: olives are pressed to produce oil
UT is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Utah

explanation.surface: An oil company is surveying the weather conditions in Utah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weather' looks like a noun about climate but is the verb meaning to come through a crisis; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a storm is to survive it, and to survive something is to last longer than it.

clue.text: Motley phraseology to lower raised spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: to lower something is to dip it
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Mixed-up wording instructs a drinker to knock back a lifted spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A simplified mixed language used between speakers of different tongues is a motley form of speech.

clue.text: Earliest browsers keep us in business

definitions.text: Earliest browsers keep us in business

indicators.note: browsers wander about, so the letters of the preceding word wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Online shops say the first people to browse their sites kept them afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'browsers' doubles as the online shoppers who sustain internet traders, so the whole clue speaks for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Online retailers depend on web browsers, people browsing their sites, to stay in business.

clue.text: Notoriety of the Italian love object with lowered head

parts.note: il is the Italian for 'the'

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is moved down a place, as if the head were lowered

parts.note: an old flame is a former object of love

explanation.surface: An Italian heartthrob, head bowed, has become notorious.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad reputation, being widely known for wrongdoing, is notoriety.

clue.text: Purple clothes are very fancy, in which bishop is one identified by pants?

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: one word dresses, i.e. surrounds, the rest

parts.note: heather is a shade of purple named after the flower
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

indicators.note: in which tells us the bishop goes inside the jumbled letters
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric is in purple robes in an elaborate scene, with a pun on underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' puts HEATHER round A plus VYRE (from 'very' via 'fancy') with B dropped inside by 'in which'. 'pants' means panting, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: An obscene phone caller is known by panting noises down the line.

clue.text: Pose upside down in lorry, arranged decoratively?

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the vehicle

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means written upwards, backwards

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone poses on their head inside a truck, as a decorative stunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done with an eye for beauty and design is creative in appearance, set out decoratively.

clue.text: Protections for Western head that is retaining engineer — quite practical

indicators.note: retaining means keeping something inside

parts.note: that is contracts to that's, written without the apostrophe
all means quite or completely, as in all alone
on means feasible, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: Gear for a cowboy's head that contains an engineer is very handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western head' means the head of a cowboy in a Western film.
explanation.definitionFit: Large wide-brimmed hats worn by cowboys protect the head, and cowboys are the Western stereotype.

clue.text: Rescript chapter in revision

indicators.note: in places one letter within the other word

parts.note: an edit is a revision

explanation.surface: A rewritten text has a chapter under revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rescript' seems to mean rewrite; it is also an official decree, especially a papal or imperial one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescript is an official order issued by a ruler, which is a decree.

clue.text: Enchantment from the writer more talented in decline

indicators.note: in places the writer and the comparative within the decline word

parts.note: to die is to decline to nothing
the writer refers to the setter, I
abler means more able, more talented

explanation.surface: A writer's magic fades even as they become more skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means sorcery or devilish magic, so it is a kind of enchantment.

clue.text: Rudimentary toes, say, all but the first inverted in flesh of calf

indicators.note: in places the turned letters within the meat

parts.note: veal is the meat of a calf

indicators.note: inverted means turned over, read backwards
the first letter is removed

parts.note: toes are an example of digits

explanation.surface: Undeveloped toes, all but one turned under, poke into calf flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but the first' drops D from DIGITS to give IGITS, and 'inverted' turns that to STIGI.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestigial organ survives only in undeveloped, rudimentary form.

clue.text: Daunting in flight

definitions.meaning: daunting means intimidating, filling with awe
split 1-4 the word means airborne, on the wing

explanation.walkthrough: Read as A-WING, like 'abed' or 'afoot', the word means flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiring awe is daunting; and the old form a-wing means in the air, flying.

clue.text: Tropical disease one's always kept away from North African

indicators.note: always kept away means every instance is removed, not just one

parts.note: beriberi is a tropical disease caused by lack of vitamin B1
one is I, and 'always' means every I goes, so both I's leave

explanation.surface: A North African who never catches tropical disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Both I's come out of BERIBERI, because 'always' extends the removal to every occurrence of 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berbers are an indigenous people of North Africa.

clue.text: Be less patient where facial sculpting is evident

definitions.meaning: split 4,4 it means hurry to a greater degree
a South Dakota mountain carved with the faces of four US presidents

explanation.definitionFit: Read in two words it means hasten more; as one name it is the mountain bearing giant presidential faces.

clue.text: Nothing in maths and French conversation belittled Japanese, perhaps

parts.note: nothing in maths is zero, the letter O
nothing in French is rien

indicators.note: belittled means made little, so the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: talk is conversation

explanation.surface: A conversation in maths and French that disparaged someone from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' does double duty: zero (O) in maths and RIEN in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Japan is from the East, so Japanese is one example of Eastern.

clue.text: Beware of bold, manipulative behaviour

parts.note: mind means beware, as in 'mind the gap'
game means bold, willing to try

explanation.surface: A warning about brash, controlling conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychological manipulation to unsettle or outwit someone is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Extremely buoyant financial district showing no change

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, its financial district
static means unchanging

explanation.surface: A very lively financial district where nothing is moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buoyant' suggests markets; here it means cheerful. The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely buoyant means overjoyed, wildly happy, which is the sense of rapturous.

clue.text: Energy consumed by Continent's food processing failure

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the other word

parts.note: Asia is a continent
pep is energy

explanation.surface: Energy used up across a continent by failures in food manufacture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'food processing' looks industrial; it means digestion.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a medical term for indigestion, a failure of the body to digest food.

clue.text: Film and another thing judiciary finally cut short

parts.note: PS, a postscript, adds 'and another thing' to a letter

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word
short means missing its final letter

parts.note: to chop is to cut

explanation.surface: A film and another matter the courts finally curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The film is Hitchcock's 1960 thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is the famous Hitchcock film, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Serious blemish on society chapter's spelling

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the spelling abbreviation sits over the society branch

parts.note: sp. is the abbreviation for spelling used in marking
a lodge is a local branch of a society such as the Freemasons

explanation.surface: A grave stain on a society branch's spelling record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' looks like literacy, but it is just the marker's abbreviation SP; 'chapter' is a Masonic lodge, not part of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A large blot or smear is a big, serious blemish.

clue.text: Irritable and eccentric, keeping one stumped

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: fey means eccentric or otherworldly
one is the Roman numeral I
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A cranky, oddball cricketer has been stumped out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter is 'stumped' when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while they are out of their ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage this word means touchy or quick-tempered, so irritable.

clue.text: Support seizing parliamentarian's beautiful place

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing and holding within

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A backer grabs an MP's lovely location.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vale of Tempe in Greece was the classical byword for a beautiful valley.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe in Thessaly was celebrated by classical poets as a lovely valley, so a place of beauty.

clue.text: Begin to work in specialist area with hospital providing cover for 14?

indicators.note: in places the setting word within the expert

parts.note: a dab, as in dab hand, is an expert
to jell is to set or come together, begin working
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Starting a job in a specialist hospital zone, someone looks for cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is BERBER; this hooded robe covers a Berber.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded woollen cloak worn in North Africa is clothing that covers a Berber.

clue.text: Down time in American plant

parts.note: down means sad, blue

explanation.surface: A melancholy spell in an American factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory; it is a small flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small North American flower with blue blossoms is a plant found in America.

clue.text: Probe into European confidence diminished Italy's former civilisation

indicators.note: into puts the probe inside the shortened word
diminished means made smaller by losing its last letter

parts.note: trust is confidence
a scan is a probe

explanation.surface: A medical probe on a European dents confidence in an ancient Italian culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diminished' cuts TRUST to TRUS, which SCAN goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Etruria formed the ancient pre-Roman civilisation of Italy.

clue.text: Distrust inflexible communications company ignoring resistance

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving the letter out

parts.note: dour means stern and unyielding
R is the physics symbol for resistance
BT is British Telecom, the UK phone company

explanation.surface: Suspicion of a rigid telecom firm that disregards opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrust is to be suspicious or uncertain about something, which is to question it.

clue.text: Process less fat, accepting piece of data that backs precautions for the sedentary

indicators.note: accepting means taking something inside
to process material is to work it into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
backs means goes backwards

parts.note: a byte is a unit of computer data

explanation.surface: A diet plan cuts fat and accepts data that supports sensible precautions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Process' reads as a verb about diets, and 'the sedentary' as idle people; they are anyone seated, as in a car. 'backs' gives ETYB, 'accepting' puts it in SAFELTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Seated travellers in cars and planes wear these restraints as a safety measure, so they are precautions.
